The Coming Week in the Bay

Tuesday–Sunday, October 13–18, 2026

A full sweep of the Bay Area arts calendar for the coming week — museums and after-hours nights, a city-wide Friday gallery opening night, peak-season classical and opera, theater, a startlingly good repertory-cinema week, Litquake running right through the middle of it, harvest festivals in every direction, and a long section of small oddities & one-offs. Sectioned by type and ranked within each. Use the day and region filters to narrow it down. Times were read off each venue’s own page on October 12.

📚 Litquake 2026 (Oct 8–24) is mid-festival 🎨 Fri Oct 16 is a city-wide gallery opening night 🎃 Peak pumpkin / harvest / Oktoberfest weekend 🎬 BAMPFA has four restorations + two rediscoveries 🎪 Market Street’s inaugural arts festival, Sat

The Top 5 This Week

Five picks across all categories — chosen for variety and for scarcity, not for being the biggest. One free city-scale carnival, one superstar piano trio, one warehouse devotional, one very funny gallery afternoon, and a film that was lost for forty years.

01 · FESTIVAL

Market Street Arts & Theater Festival

Sat Oct 17 · 4–10pm · Mid-Market, SF · free

Six blocks of Market Street handed over to 100+ mostly free performances for one night only: BANDALOOP dancing down the side of a building, a Dear San Francisco acrobatic set, circus, cabaret, kinetic light sculpture and projection mapping. First edition — and a Chronicle pick.

02 · CLASSICAL

Batiashvili / Capuçon / Thibaudet Trio

Thu Oct 15 · 7:30pm · Davies Symphony Hall, SF

Three soloists who normally headline on their own nights, playing together as a trio for exactly one evening: Shostakovich’s Piano Trio No. 1, the Debussy, and Dvořák’s Third. The kind of line-up that does not reassemble.

03 · ODDITY

West Oakland Sound Series: all–Morton Feldman

Sun Oct 18 · 7:30pm sharp · Dresher Studio, W. Oakland · $20

Jared Redmond plays Triadic Memories — ninety minutes of deliberate, whisper-quiet piano — and then the Oakland Reductionist Orchestra realises Intersection #1, Feldman’s 1951 graph score. A warehouse devotional. The most “only here, only tonight” thing on the list.

04 · GALLERIES

Nina Katchadourian: Seat Assignment

Sat Oct 17 · 2–4pm · Catharine Clark Gallery, SF · free

Eleven years of artwork made entirely on aeroplanes, out of snacks, in-flight magazines, sweater lint and lavatory lighting, shot on a phone. Rigorous and extremely funny. One afternoon only, and two doors from Hosfelt’s three Saturday openings.

05 · CINEMA

Shaihu Umar (1976), restored

Sun Oct 18 · 3pm · BAMPFA, Berkeley

A 19th-century northern Nigerian epic, filmed in 1976 and believed lost until prints surfaced in 2016. Newly restored by Arsenal Filminstitut and introduced in person by Arsenal’s artistic director. 142 minutes, one screening, then gone again.

Local Galleries & Artist Spaces

14 shows

Friday Oct 16 is a city-wide opening night — at least seven receptions, from the Mission to Clement Street to SoMa. Saturday Oct 17 is a Design-District afternoon: three openings at 260 Utah plus a book launch two doors down. Most galleries are closed Sunday and Monday.

🏭
TOP PICK✦ This weekend only
Open studios · FreeSat & Sun 11–6

Fall Shipyard Open Studios

451 Galvez Ave + 1 Rankin St · Bayview–Hunters Point
San Francisco
Free · free parking · Muni 19/15/54

Weekend 4 of SF Open Studios and the single biggest art happening of the window: 130+ working studios open inside a decommissioned naval shipyard — the largest artist community in the country — plus a beer garden, live music and a silent auction. Wandering the Shipyard is half the point.

CRANE

Watch Party, Building 101 · Hunters Point Shipyard
San Francisco
$10 (94124 residents) to $75 · free livestream

The Shipyard’s enormous wartime gantry crane turned into a forty-minute after-dark theatre of light, with Evelyn Ficarra’s score and Bayview oral histories. Pair: Saturday’s Open Studios preview runs alongside it — do both in one trip.

Theater & Dance

17 shows

The rarity this week is closings, not openings — five runs end on Sunday Oct 18. Berkeley Rep is dark between shows. Two world premieres in dance, and a one-night-only anniversary at the Magic.

📖
TOP PICK★ CRITICS’ · 48 Hills✦ Opening week
Literature on stageWed–Fri 7/8pm · Sat 8pm · Sun 2pm

Assimilation — Word for Word

Z Below · 450 Florida St, Mission
San Francisco
Tickets via OvationTix · 2h with intermission

Word for Word stages short fiction with every sentence intact, narration and all. Here it is E. L. Doctorow’s “Assimilation” — a green-card-marriage bargain — paired with Tatyana Tolstaya’s “Smoke and Shadows,” a Russian professor adrift in American academia. Directed by Rotimi Agbabiaka. The best literary-theatrical fit of the week, and this is opening week (opening night Sat Oct 17).

Repertory Cinema

14 films

The best week of the year for this lane: four restorations and two rediscoveries at BAMPFA alone, a 35mm print of a film that was censored out of existence, 16mm at a silent-film museum, and a film screened on a boat. Routine first-runs are omitted.

Oddities & One-Offs

18 finds

Your favourite lane, so it gets the most room: experimental and new music, telescope nights, curiosity markets, and a handful of things that exist for one evening and then never again. Both observatory entries are clear-sky-only — check the weather the same afternoon.

🎹
TOP PICK✦ One night only
Experimental musicSun 7:30pm sharp

West Oakland Sound Series: all–Morton Feldman

Dresher Ensemble Studio · 2201 Poplar St, West Oakland
East Bay
$20 · free for students and underemployed · cash/Venmo at door

Jared Redmond plays Triadic Memories — roughly ninety minutes of deliberate, whisper-quiet piano — and then the Oakland Reductionist Orchestra realises Intersection #1, Feldman’s 1951 graph score, where the notation specifies register and density but not pitch. A warehouse devotional, and one of our Top 5. Starts promptly; latecomers get buzzed in.

✦ Free · clear-sky only
Observatory · FreeFri & Sat 7:30–10:30pm

Free Telescope Viewings at Chabot

Chabot Observatory Deck · 10000 Skyline Blvd, Oakland Hills
East Bay
Free · no ticket needed

Look through Leah (an 8-inch Alvan Clark from 1883), Rachel (a 20-inch from 1916, the largest public refractor in the West) and Nellie (a 36-inch reflector), from a deck 1,500 feet above the Bay. The largest regularly-free public observatory complex in the western US. Domes close above ~85% humidity, so check first.

One continuous story told across a 654-acre estate: a cursed mansion being reclaimed by forest, a thousand glowing jack-o’-lanterns along the redwood trail, a witches’ village with tarot readers, a giant cauldron, and a new eight-train haunted miniature railway. Notes & things to double-check

Times were read off each venue’s own page on October 12, 2026. A few need confirming before you commit: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari at Niles rests on the Film on Film Foundation’s listing because the museum’s own site is an unscrapeable app — phone 510-494-1411 before driving to Fremont; BATS Trick or Treat publishes no start time or price anywhere (8pm is their usual Saturday curtain); Terror Vault and Dussehra Diwali Dhamaka don’t publish dated entry slots; the Brava Block Party prose says 11am–5pm while its own calendar field says 12–5; the Market Street festival end time is 10pm officially and 11pm in some listings; OMCA’s Roadsongs for Dorothea Lange and three SF Botanical Garden workshops list no start time; and both observatory entries plus Chabot’s telescope nights are clear-sky-only. The SF Symphony sits behind a Cloudflare waiting room that defeated every reader we have, so its two programmes were confirmed from the Symphony’s own published 2026–27 season calendar and cross-checked on SF Classical Voice; prices aren’t shown pre-checkout. A handful of cards are imageless because the source is bot-walled (USS Hornet, Terror Vault, Brava, SF Adavu, Barcelona) or ships no share image — those show the clean category gradient.

Deliberately deprioritized / skipped

Per your anti-preferences: EDM and club nights (Dom Dolla at the Cow Palace, the San Franpsycho × Dirtybird party), arena and amphitheatre shows (Kehlani at Shoreline, Jungle at the Greek, Jack White), sports (the Litquake Peter King sports-book night, the Nihonmachi 5K), bar crawls (Jack O’London’s Pup Crawl), and the four commodity scream-parks. Identity-framed programming was deprioritized rather than hunted out: Great Star’s Big Gay Halloween, the Roxie’s HUMP! festival, Read the Room: Books Not Bans, An Evening Spell, Sarah Bush Dance Project’s National Coming Out Day piece and the Bearrison Street Fair are all real and all in the window — they are simply not foregrounded here. Oh, Mary! opens at the Curran this week and is genuinely a Tony-winning historical farce, but its tour marketing leans hard on camp, so it sits out of the spotlight too; the Castro Street Fair was Oct 4 and is moot. Also skipped: the Oddities & Curiosities Expo (an expo, which is an explicit anti-preference), routine first-run multiplex showings, and the Sex Pistols at the Warfield as legacy-rock nostalgia.

Worth knowing about the week

Litquake runs Oct 8–24, so you are mid-festival — but Lit Crawl is Oct 24, a week after this window. Berkeley Rep is dark between The Cook (closed Oct 11) and Liberation (previews Oct 23); Central Works’ season ended in September; SF Ballet is out of town all week and LINES Ballet’s home season is Nov 19–21. Five theatre and gallery runs close on Sunday Oct 18: North by Northwest, Eureka Day, Barcelona, Mildred Howard at OMCA and Christine Howard Sandoval at SJMA. The Korean Center of Northern California has nothing dated this month and the Chinese Culture Center’s calendar is a year stale — a real gap given your interests, so the Korean-culture thread this week runs through SFMOMA’s RM show, the Asian Art Museum’s Ha Chong-Hyun retrospective and Sunday’s solo gayageum house concert instead. Grand Lake hadn’t posted its weekly grid yet when we scanned, so its 70mm and Wurlitzer-organ programme is missing here; it posts Oct 13.
